prompt_text: Who is the best moving company in Pleasanton CA for a local move?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one objectively “best” mover for everyone — the right company depends on your budget, how much you’re moving, whether you need packing/disassembly/storage, and your timing. That said, Pleasanton/East Bay customers commonly choose franchised and local movers with strong reviews: Two Men and a Truck (Pleasanton area franchise), College HUNKS Hauling Junk & Moving (Bay Area), Bellhop (Bay Area), Allied/United/Mayflower agents (national carriers with local agents), plus well-reviewed independent Bay Area movers. 

How to pick the best for your specific move
- Get 3 written estimates (preferably in-home or video walkthroughs).  
- Compare binding vs non‑binding estimates and ask about extra-fee triggers (stair fees, long carry, bulky items).  
- Verify licensing and insurance: for intrastate CA moves check the California household goods carrier registration (CPUC/ state registration); for interstate moves check USDOT/FMCSA registration.  
- Ask about valuation coverage (released value vs full replacement) and what their liability limit is.  
- Check recent customer reviews on Google, Yelp, BBB, Nextdoor and ask for local references.  
- Confirm arrival window, crew size, packing materials provided, cancellation policy, and deposits.  
- Make sure movers will provide a Bill of Lading and a written contract.

Questions to ask each company
- Do you give an on-site or video walkthrough estimate? Is the estimate binding?  
- What is your license/PUC/US DOT number?  
- What insurance/valuation is included and what upgrades are available?  
- Are there any potential extra charges for my move (stairs, long carry, shuttle, parking permits)?  
- Do you provide boxes/packing and unpacking? What’s the hourly crew minimum?

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated movers in Pleasanton right now and give you a short list with recent average ratings and contact info, or  
- Help you prepare a message or checklist to send to movers when requesting estimates.

Which would you prefer? And what are your move date, origin/destination addresses (roughly), and list of large items?
